text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

Hi A, C asked me to help with the leaking espresso machine/grinder situation. I’m not asking for a solution or a decision yet. I heard you may want a simpler machine; I’d like to understand it in your own words: What matters to you about that, and why? Is there anything about the leak, the grinder, or how this gets handled that matters to you too? If anything is hard to say because it might create tension, you can tell me just the need; I won’t treat silence as agreement, and I’ll check again before treating anything as settled.

I’m also a participant here, so I have one concern I’d like to put on the list only if it fits for you: “That each person has room to say what matters to them and why.” Does that wording fit? Please tell me if even a small part doesn’t, or if you disagree with me including it; I won’t record it unless you say it fits.

I suppose what matters is having something simple that doesn’t keep demanding attention—I’m pretty worn out after long days, and I don’t have the energy to take on repairs, a cleaning rota, or a drawn-out discussion. The leak does matter, and I’d hope any way of handling it doesn’t leave that ongoing work to me. I’m not sure what I think about the grinder specifically. Your wording fits; having room to say what matters without it being treated as agreement is important.

At the end, one brief check-in where each person can say what matters and any even-minor discomfort; no one is treated as having agreed by silence. C is not in the middle; I keep the list.
